content: Beclin-1 is a protein in humans encoded by the BECN1 gene. It is the mammalian ortholog of the yeast autophagy-related gene 6 (Atg6) and the BEC-1 gene in the nematode C. elegans. This protein interacts with either BCL-2 or PI3K class III, playing a pivotal role in regulating both autophagy and cell death. Beclin-1 is critically involved in disease processes, including tumorigenesis and neurodegeneration, as it is a key component of the autophagic programmed cell death pathway. In ovarian cancer, increased autophagy is associated with less aggressive tumor behavior and improved responsiveness to chemotherapy. In contrast, schizophrenia is linked to reduced levels of Beclin-1 in the hippocampus, which leads to impaired autophagy and, consequently, increased neuronal cell death.
